Credential chip

.dr-chip · --claim · --sm · .dr-chips · --stack · components/badge.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

Verified by DRON
  1. 1.dr-chipsThe row that holds credentials: wraps, gap 6.
  2. 2.dr-chipThe pill: --r-pill, padding 5 / 10, 12/600, gap 6. Measured 164.1 × 26.8 for Verified by DRON.
  3. 3.dr-ic:first-childThe leading mark, 14px: a shield with the check inside it for a claim DRON confirmed.
  4. 4.dr-ic:last-childThe trailing tick, 14px. It says confirmed rather than merely stated, so the chip is never reduced to its colour.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Verification badge.

When to use

The credential chip answers RJ-C1, the highest single drop-off in the CJM: confirm the operator is real and qualified. So the credentials sit on the operator card, beside the name and job count and before any tap, never on a profile page behind a click. They stand on tracking, order-confirmed, account, operator-account, operator-listings and inspection-report. The same chip family also carries plain facts on review cards and, at --sm, a role beside a name.

The rule reads in one line: green means DRON confirmed this document, grey means a plain supporting fact. Green is the tint behind a charcoal label, never the letters, so the chip does not break the fill-only rule; it is the rule. The shield with a check, the plain shield and the trailing tick make the difference legible in drawing as well as in colour (WCAG 1.4.1). A --trust blue rung for third-party confirmation is declared in the ui/kit.css archive and drawn nowhere; it was not ported into components/.

The words are facts, not adjectives: Verified by DRON, Insured, CAA licence. On order-confirmed-empty alone the claim is shortened to Verified so the pair fits one row.

Sources: DESIGN.md § Chips and badges · § Named rules (One Accent) · inventory.md § 1 (Verification badge) · microcopy.md § order-confirmed, tracking · voice.md P2

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Andriy M.4.9 ★ · 214 jobsVerified by DRONInsured

Credentials on the card, under the name they vouch for, readable without a tap.

Don’t

Book again

A chip used as a control. A chip states a fact and takes no tap; an action is a button, and an applied filter that can be removed is the filter chip of in-page tabs. A state that changes, such as availability, is the availability badge.
